title: Styles and Content Projection
summary: Scoped styling, passing markup into a component, and reaching its elements.
heading: Styles and Content Projection

blocks.text: A component's styles only affect that component's own template. So a .title rule in one component won't accidentally restyle a .title somewhere else. Angular keeps each component's CSS to itself — this is called view encapsulation.

blocks.label: card.css

blocks.text: Sometimes a component is a wrapper — like a card — and you want to drop your own content inside it. <ng-content> marks the slot where that content lands.

blocks.caption: Markup you write between the tags drops into the ng-content slot.

blocks.label: card.ts (the wrapper)

blocks.text: Now and then you need a real element from your template — to focus an input, for example. Mark it with a reference (Chapter 20) and grab it with viewChild.

blocks.label: search.ts

blocks.text: Reach for this only when you truly need the element. Most of the time, bindings and signals already do what you want.

items: Component styles are scoped to that component only.
<ng-content> is a slot for markup passed in from outside.
Whatever you put between the component's tags lands in that slot.
viewChild grabs an element from the template when you need it.
Prefer bindings and signals first; use queries sparingly.
